content: 1. Elagolix and Erlotinib: Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of erlotinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. Consider increasing the dose of erlotinib if necessary. 2. Elagolix and Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Erythromycin increases elagolix levels via mechanisms involving P-glycoprotein (MDR1) and CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of adverse effects. 3. Elagolix and Escitalopram: Elagolix increases escitalopram levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 and decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 4. Elagolix and Eslicarbazepine Acetate: Eslicarbazepine decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Elagolix and Esomeprazole: Elagolix increases esomeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 and decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 6. Elagolix and Estradiol, Estrogens (Conjugated, Esterified), Ethinyl Estradiol, Estropipate: Elagolix decreases the levels of these estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Estrogen-containing contraceptives may reduce elagolix efficacy. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended during and for one week after elagolix treatment. 7. Elagolix and Ethosuximide: Elagolix decreases ethosuximide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 8. Elagolix and Etoposide: Elagolix reduces etoposide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Elagolix and Etravirine: Etravirine decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4, while elagolix increases etravirine levels by inhibiting CYP2C19. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 10. Elagolix and Everolimus: Elagolix increases everolimus levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) and decreases them by inducing CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 11. Elagolix and Exemestane: Elagolix decreases exemestane levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 12. Elagolix and Exenatide: Exenatide slows gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption of oral medications like elagolix. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide administration. 13. Elagolix and Fedratinib: Fedratinib increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4, while elagolix decreases fedratinib levels by inducing CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Elagolix and Felbamate: Elagolix reduces felbamate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 15. Elagolix and Felodipine: Elagolix decreases felodipine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 16. Elagolix and Fenofibrate (Micronized, Fenofibric Acid): Elagolix reduces fenofibrate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 17. Elagolix and Fentanyl (Intranasal, Transdermal, Transmucosal): Elagolix decreases fentanyl levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 18. Elagolix and Fexinidazole: Fexinidazole increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Co-administration is not recommended. Use alternative drugs. 19. Elagolix and Fexofenadine: Elagolix increases fexofenadine levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Elagolix and Finerinone: Elagolix increases finerinone levels by inhibiting CYP2E1. Co-administration is not recommended. Use alternative drugs. 21. Elagolix and Flibanserin: Elagolix increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 and decreases them by inducing CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 22. Elagolix and Flurazepam: Elagolix decreases flurazepam levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 23. Elagolix and Flutamide: Elagolix reduces flutamide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 24. Elagolix and Fosamprenavir: Elagolix decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 25. Elagolix and Fosaprepitant: Elagolix reduces fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 26. Elagolix and Fosphenytoin: Elagolix increases fosphenytoin levels by inhibiting CYP2C19, while fosphenytoin decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended.
